On their turn a player may either replicate a piece by moving one square away into an empty space and leaving the original piece, or jump a piece two squares away into an empty space (losing the original piece). After the move, any opponent’s pieces adjacent to the destination are converted to the moving player’s colour. Play continues until all squares are filled or one player has no pieces; the winner is the player with the most pieces remaining.

39594.overview: Stadium Cross is excellent motocross racing game from Sega was produced in 1992.

39605.overview:
Star Fire II was produced by Exidy in 1979.

Unreleased sequel to Star Fire with very simular gameplay and changes that mainly involved high score enhancements and sharpening of graphics. Presumably just suppossed to be a ROM upgrade.

39608.overview:
Star Guards was produced by Bally Midway in 1986.

Players control robot warriors fighting enemies in outer space.

39615.overview:
Star Soldier: Vanishing Earth (スターソルジャー バニシングアース Sutā Sorujā Banishingu Āsu) is a 1998 shoot 'em up video game developed and published by Hudson Soft (Electro Brain for the North American release) for the Nintendo 64. It is a direct sequel to Soldier Blade and part of their Star Soldier series. A arcade version was released for the Seta's Aleck64 Arcade board, which possessed hardware similar to the Nintendo 64.

Star Soldier: Vanishing Earth brings back most of the staple gameplay systems from previous titles back, with some changes and additions. Players can now pick up between three different ships, each with its own strengths and weaknesses. This games ditches the ability of swapping weapons during gameplay, as weapon types are now tied to each ship. Aside of the main weapon and smart bombs (here called Ex-Arms, of which each ship has two different ones), the ships also have a new Rolling maneuver, a defensive move which makes the ship briefly invincible and deflects enemy bullets.

39618.overview:
Star Trek: Voyager — The Arcade Game is a first-person style shooter arcade game, manufactured by Monarch Entertainment and Team Play Inc. and released in 2002.

Star Trek: Voyager — The Arcade Game is a light gun game played from the first-person shooter perspective. The player uses a light gun which can be aimed and fired at on-screen enemies. The reloading process is referred to as remodulation, a term used in Star Trek, and is done by shooting the gun off-screen.

Much of the game takes place on the USS Voyager, shooting various alien intruders such as the Borg, Hirogen Hunters, Species 8472 as well as several other alien species from the Star Trek universe. The game has several missions players can select as the game progresses. Some missions involve flight in the Delta Flyer, one of the shuttles used by the crew of the USS Voyager. During these sequences players attack Borg vessels such as Borg Cubes and Spheres.

39619.overview:
Star Trigon is a video game developed by Namco. Star Trigon puts the player in the role of a spaceperson spinning around a planet, having to rescue the stranded aliens in time before his air supply runs out. Games in this series have been released for iPod, Windows, and iPhone in addition to the arcade versions.

In Star Trigon, after a character and stage is selected the player has to rescue stranded aliens from aimlessly drifting through outer space by hopping from planet to planet to form triangles, the alien is saved if the player manages to contain a drifting alien within a triangle. The player will be awarded in-game pickups to increase score and air packets to increase air supply. Star Trigon is simple in only requiring one button, the challenge is timing the jumps from planet to planet and rescuing the stranded aliens before the air supply is depleted and as your characters are spinning faster and faster without jumping off screen. Along the way new obstacles will help complicate things and add to the challenge of the game like black holes and flares.

39629.overview:
Steal See is a rare and obscure puzzle arcade game developed by Moov Generation and published by Eolith in 2000.

The game features a unique "Steal See" puzzle mode where players reveal parts of a hidden backdrop image. It also includes a secondary mode called "Get Land," which plays similarly to the classic adult arcade game Gals Panic.

39630.overview: Steel Force is a 2D top down arcade shooter, similar in style to Alien Breed, but much more action-oriented. The main hero, a Federation soldier fights against space pirates - he must kill various enemies and find the exit in limited time. He can find ammunition, health packs and various power ups along the way.

39631.overview: A very important professor and his daughter have been kidnapped by terrorists and it is up to you and a friend to play as Garcia and Cliff to rescue them. The game is a 1st person perspective rail-shooter where you use a gun to shoot wave after waves of baddies trying to kill you. The game forces you to follow a set path and will scroll in various directions and also stop to allow you to destroy a wave of baddies. There are various types of baddies from foot soldiers to huge flying robots. As well as infinite bullets you also have a limited supply of missiles which destroy everything on screen, but be careful not to shoot ordinary civilians as they will lose part of your energy bar which also decreases when hit by bullets and missiles. When your energy bar is empty then it's game over but you can continue where you last died. At the end of a stage you face a end of stage baddy who requires multiple shots to destroy.

39632.overview:
Steel Gunner 2 is a gun mounted shooting gallery game for one or two players, and it is the sequel to Steel Gunner. Once again, players take the role of Neo Arc policemen, Garcia and Cliff, and this time they are on a mission to destroy the evil army of Vanguard who are attacking the city. 

Use the light guns to shoot down robots and avoid hitting citizens. There is an on-screen sight for aiming, infinite ammo and a limited amount missiles. Most background objects are interactive, meaning that players can shoot and destroy parked cars, glass windows, street signs even destroy entire buildings. The game uses parallax scrolling and sprite scaling effects with enemies and grenades flying toward the screen and pseudo 3D tunnel sections.

There are 6 levels although the game doesn't display typical "level 1" texts, each level ends with the players entering a flying cargo ship that repairs some damage and supplies extra weapons. The game starts in a shopping mall and city streets (level 1), then through subway tunnels and into an abandoned warehouse (level 2), across open sea to an industrial island (level 3), into the industrial complex (level 4), back onto the city streets chasing a giant Independence Day-like spaceship (level 5) and finally inside the giant spaceship (level 6).

39633.overview:
Steel Talons brought realism-oriented helicopter combat to the arcades, and later to home systems. The action is viewed from behind your helicopter, with the 3D polygon world rotating around you, taking in mountains, rivers and deserts. 

There are 12 missions in total, each of which requires you to destroy targets in a set time limit. There are also training and head-to-head (against a CPU-controlled drone) modes. 

You have a limited number of automatically-targeting missiles as well as a cannon. A tracking map tells you where you are on the level, and where the enemies are. Contact with the ground, mountains or other vehicles will damage or destroy your helicopter.

39635.overview: Steep Slope Sliders is an ST-V based snowboarding game developed by Cave Co., ltd and published by Capcom. In comparison to other snowboarding games being released in the same time frame, particularly Cool Boarders, Steep Slope Sliders utilized a unique trick system, colorful characters, and an optional real time clock-based system for determining the proper time of day at each location.

39647.overview:
Storm Blade was produced by Visco Corporation in 1996.

Storm Blade is a military themed vertical scrolling shoot 'em up game where you take control of either Lucky J. Striker in his F14 Tomcat, Alex in his MiG-29 Fulcrum, Camel Yuki Anderson in her AV-BB Harrier II or old man Isoroku Kaionji in his Zero Fighter Kamikaze Special. Each with their own weapons patrons.

As you make progress and fight of various planes, helicopters, tanks, static guns, ships and bosses power-ups come available. Power-ups cans can be collected from destroyed enemies and increase your firepower. These come in two forms: a normal power-up (P) and a super power-up (F). There are also a limited number of super bombs available that do a vast amount of damage. Destroyed enemies sometimes drop additional super bombs (B). The game can be played solo or with a friend.

39651.overview: In this comical maze game, the player controls a nude streaker girl who runs around a city maze and she must eat all foods shaped circle while must pick up all the clothes and accessories and back to dress for avoid being caught by the police officers, she also may escape quickly using orbed portals located at each corner of the maze.

39659.overview:
Street Fighter III: 2nd Impact: Giant Attack is the follow-up to Street Fighter III: New Generation. The brothers Yun and Yang are now truly separate characters with different moves, the demonic Akuma known from previous Street Fighter installments returns (though not as regular part of the roster), and two other new characters are introduced: Hugo, a gigantic professional wrestler, and Urien, the brother of the boss character, Gill.

There are also some notable additions in terms of gameplay. A player can now perform EX Specials, which are powered up versions of the moves at the cost of a reduced Super Art gauge. It's possible to escape from a throwing attack, and a "Personal Action" grants characters specific benefits (Alex receives more attack power for example). Furthermore, there is now a bonus round which tests the parrying skill of the player, as Sean throws basketballs towards him which can be deflected.

39660.overview:
Street Fighter III: 3rd Strike: Fight for the Future is the second updated version of Street Fighter III which adds new characters, new music, storylines, more super arts for each character, a grading system, a manual throw system, and path selection. The most significant change is the introduction of the guard parry, which helps defend against multi-hit combos.

This version adds five new characters to the rosters such as Chun Li (from Street Fighter II), Makoto (a judo expert), Twelve (another Gill clone), Q (who resembles a Japanese superhero similar to Tetsujin 28) and Remy (a Guile/Nash clone). This game also marks the return of bonus rounds which were last present in Super Street Fighter II.

39663.overview: Street Fighter Zero 3 Upper is an updated version of Street Fighter Zero 3 (also known as Street Fighter Alpha 3). The game was released on the Sega Naomi hardware rather than the original games CPSII hardware. The updated version includes all the added characters from the console versions of Street Fighter Zero 3. Additional characters include Fei-Long, Dee Jay, T Hawk, Guile, Evil Ryu and Shin Akuma.

39669.overview: Axel, Adam and Blaze - ex-cops, the solution to punk pollution. The city's a war zone, and they're going out two at a time to give the gangs a kick in the guts. This is the ultimate in street combat. These city fighters are martial arts maniacs with a battery of individually controllable attacks - including jabs, head butts, and overhead kicks. They're up against a mob of Kung-Fu creeps and axe-hurling fiends. On the streets it's only two of them against hordes of attacking scum. Slam into pipe-wielding weirdos and bash 'em with their own metal. Throw an uppercut or an elbow smash - these goons keep comin'!

39670.overview: After Axel Stone, Blaze Fielding and Adam Hunter destroyed the evil Syndicate leader, Mr. X, the city became a peaceful place to live, and each one of them followed their own paths. One year later, after their reunion, Adam's brother Sammy returned from school to find their apartment in a mess, and Adam nowhere to be seen, and after calling his two friends, one of them notices a photo of Adam chained to a wall, next to someone they knew very well - Mr. X, who returned to turn the peaceful city once again into a war zone. Now, Axel, Blaze, Sammy, and Axel's good friend Max, a pro wrestler, must head out to stop Mr. X once again...hopefully for good...

39671.overview:
Strength & Skill - Guiness Book of Records was produced by Sun Electronics and Kitco in 1984.

A sports game from Sun Electronics and Kitco.

39678.overview:
Strike Gunner S.T.G is a vertical scrolling shoot 'em up video game originally released on the arcades in 1991 by Tecmo, and then later ported for the SNES.

The player takes control of a high-tech jet, the "Strike Gunner" of the title, and faces wave after wave of enemies, ranging from helicopters, jets, tanks and airships, among others. On the first screen you select your secondary item like sheilds, homing missiles. etc.

39681.overview:
Strike Zone Baseball was produced by Leland in 1988.

Strike Zone Baseball is an action-oriented baseball game with the DOS version starring the baseball star Orel Hershiser.

This game offers 2 modes of play - strike zone (main game), and home run derby (batting training). This gameplay is made up for by animations of baseball players, and user interface that allows you to adjust both the speed and direction of your bat with on-screen gauges The player can choose among 26 teams and play directly in the positions of batter and pitcher. A managerial element is also included: when playing a whole season the player can choose the lineup and the batting order.

39684.overview:
Stunt Air is an Action game, developed and published by Nuova Videotron, which was released in Europe in 1983.

The game is a hacked/modded version of Sega's Star Jacker.

39688.overview:
A one or two player shooter game published and developed by Sigma Enterprises in 1985.

The player takes control of a futuristic submarine and must shoot their way through the game's levels in a underwater city and in the depths of the seabed and it is attacked from both sides beneath the water in which the submarine moves and from the bottom the water, by a variety of enemies you must destroy all the machines and avoid collide with obstacles while you pick captive divers and fuel to reach the end of level.

39692.overview:
For generations, people have believed in the Chinese myth known as the Dark Legend. It occurs sometime in the 11th or 12th century when China plunges into a state of total anarchy, when power-hungry warlords rebel against the central government. To regain control over his empire, the emperor devises a cunning plan. He prepares for the ultimate conquest for his most ambitious rivals, a challenge that no warlord is able to resist as the rewards are unimaginable. The victor will be endowed with incredible abilities and possess ultimate power, not to mention unlimited wealth. The triumph is absolute as defeat means death. Thousands of fearless warriors battle among themselves with special fighting abilities.

The game takes place in Liangshan Marsh, where 12 of the strongest outlaws out of 108 gather to test their battle skills against each other while the Gods of War watch from above. The characters are inspired by the 108 outlaws from the Chinese classical novel Water Margin by Shi Naian.

39707.overview:
Super Astro Fighter was produced by Data East in 1982.

A simple space shooter from Data East.

39713.overview:
Super Bike was produced by Century Electronics in 1983.


Steer, jump and shoot skulls as you drive your motorbike. Burst balloons for bonus points.

39718.overview: An advanced version of a classic type of game. Moni & Chris are on a quest to rid there island of viscous invading monsters. Players blow bubble to entrap the monsters and then jump on them to make them pop. Luckily Moni & Chris have many items to help them dispose of these dangerous foes. Like exterminate scrolls which called forth the force of the elements and nature or the super transform crystal which powers up our heroes so they don't have to encase the enemies in bubbles first they can just run into they to destroy them. Players can in power up the attack button to blow a triple bubble instead of a single. The main objective of the players is to clear all the enemies for each area of the island. The game consists of 4 chapters with 60 stages.

39728.overview:
Super Chase: Criminal Termination is an arcade racing game, released in 1992 by Taito. It is the third release in the Chase H.Q. arcade series, and the sequel to Special Criminal Investigation.

It also was the first in the Chase H.Q. series to have the protagonist command the car from a first-person view, and have different vehicles available to drive. Nancy, the dispatcher from Chase H.Q. returns, this time, on a videoscreen inside the car before the start of the stage.

39732.overview: Super Cross II is a one or two player motocross racing game published and developed by GM Shoji in 1986.

39733.overview: Super Crowns Golf is a retro sports arcade game released in 1989. It was developed and published by Nasco Japan. The game serves as the third entry in the Crowns Golf trilogy, succeeding the original Crowns Golf (1984) and Crowns Golf in Hawaii (1985).

39749.overview:
Super Eagle Shot was released by SETA in 1994.

A golfing game for up to four players from SETA.

39750.overview:
Super Football Champ was produced by Taito in 1996.

Super Football Champ is a video game available on Arcade and PSone, sports genre, developed by Taito Corporation and published by Taito Corporation.

39752.overview:
Super Free Kick was produced by HaesungHJ Corp. in 1988.

A Breakout style game with a soccer theme.

39754.overview:
The Super Game III is a bootleg multi-game arcade system released in 1992 by the South Korean company Seo Jin.

Similar to Nintendo’s official PlayChoice-10 arcade cabinets, it allowed players to select from a menu of console games and play them for a limited time per coin.

The system contained 15 pirated Famicom games. To obscure their bootleg nature, many of these titles featured modified color palettes, edited text, or altered title logos. These included classics and heavily edited variants like:
• Super Mario Bros. 3
• Super Mary (a bootleg edit of Super Mario Bros.)
• King Kong (a hack of Donkey Kong Jr.)
• Gorilla 3
• Popular arcade-to-home ports like Bomberman, Pac-Man, Galaga, Excitebike, and Mappy.

39755.overview:
The Super Game Mega Type 1 (often abbreviated as sgmt1) is a bootleg multi-game arcade system released in 1994 by a manufacturer known as Kim. It is not a standard standalone cabinet, but rather an unlicenced hardware modification (hacked clone) of a Nintendo PlayChoice-10 arcade board, built using components derived from the Nintendo Entertainment System (NES) and Famicom hardware architecture.

Unlike legitimate commercial multi-game systems that featured dozens of options, the Super Game Mega Type 1 hardware was built to support exactly 7 platform-style games. To bypass standard limitations of the clone hardware, it utilized large 2-megabit (or greater) memory sizes to host a collection of prominent NES titles:
1. Rockman 5 (Mega Man 5)
2. Ninja 2 (Ninja Ryukenden / Ninja Gaiden)

39757.overview:
The Glob (also known as Super Glob and Beastie Feastie) is an arcade game released by Epos in 1983.

Guide the insatiable Glob through corridors, up and down the elevators and through the side tunnels in his never-ending search for snacks. An assortment of crafty animals relentlessly pursue the Glob and fight him for control of the elevators. Kill them by sticking to the ceiling and dropping on them or just avoid them and munch a dozen different snacks to clear the 24 unique levels.

This game is nearly identical to the later release Beastie Feastie. Cardinal Amusement Products, who produced Beastie Feastie, was a division of EPOS Corporation.
This game was cloned as The Glob and Beastie Feastie.

39762.overview: Super High Impact was one of the most hard hitting football games before the NFL Blitz series was created, with 18 teams and over 30 plays per team. The console versions are based on the Midway arcade series of the same name. The game has a Hit-O-Meter which often leads to massive brawls. Based on the arcade smash hit back in the days, featuring the three famous words: EAT THIS!!!, FIGHT!!!

39769.overview:
Super Lup Lup in an action/puzzle game in which different coloured marbles continually roll down a spiral path towards a central goal line. 

Players control a rotating cannon situated at the center of the spiral and must stop the line of marbles from reaching the goal by shooting matching coloured marbles into the line. If three or more marbles of the same colour are matched, they will disappear. 

In addition to standard marbles, bonus items occasionally appear that will, for example, temporarily slow down the rate the marbles' advance. Also, providing there is a clear line of sight, unwanted marbles can be fired straight out of the play area to prevent them from adding to the advancing line. All marbles must be destroyed to complete a level. The game is over once the marbles are pushed over the goal threshold.

The game is an unofficial clone of the Mitchell game "Puzz Loop", with the main difference being that the dip settings of "Super Lup Lup" can be set to display photos of naked men or women.

39773.overview:
The Princess has been kidnapped by the evil Bowser, and it is up to Mario and brother Luigi to save the day.

The first ever platform adventure for the Mario Brothers has the player exploring level after level, with Bowser to contend with as the end of level boss. Power-ups include the Super Mushroom, which increases Mario's size and power, the fire flower, allowing him to shoot fireballs at enemies, and the ever important starman for a short burst of invincibility.

Each level includes a bonus section filled with coins plus a shortcut through the level, plenty of bad buys and obstacles to get past, and an end of level flag, in which the higher the player grabs it, the more points are awarded to them. Certain levels also include warp points, which takes the player to higher levels.

39786.overview:
Super Monaco GP was produced by Sega in 1989.

Super Monaco GP is a first-person perspective racing game which allows you to race other cars around the famous Monaco Grand Prix course. You first must qualify for a position on the grid by driving round a shortened version of the course on your own. The faster you drive the higher placing on the grid. The actual race has you competing against 19 other drivers and as well as trying to beat them all you must get to checkpoints within a time limit or it is race over. You also have to stay ahead of a certain position which starts at 20th and gets lower the longer the race goes on.

The Genesis version of Super Monaco adds a complete career mode, however. In the career mode, your goal is to win a season of races. Unfortunately, you start with a relatively slow car. By challenging other drivers, you can move to a better team and car, and ultimately win the F1 World Title. As well as the famous Monaco course, others from around the world have been added, to give the game a longer shelf life.

39804.overview:
Super Punch-Out!! is a boxing game where you attempt to defeat five different champions, Bear Hugger, Dragon Chan, Vodka Drunkenski, Great Tiger and Super Macho Man. If you defeat all five, you become the champion and defend your title against the same five characters.

Similar to Punch-Out!! but now the player can duck by pulling up -- not merely pressing up -- on the joystick. This move is required to dodge Super Macho Man's special punch and Dragon Chan's Jumping Kick from the turnbuckles.

39816.overview:
Super Real Mahjong PIV is a Japanese strip mahjong arcade video game developed and published by SETA Corporation. Released in April 1993, it stands as the fourth main entry in the popular Super Real Mahjong arcade franchise. The game is famous for its high-quality anime style graphics and its classic "win to undress" gameplay format.

Players compete in standard 1-on-1 mahjong matches against female opponents. Winning a hand makes the opponent remove a layer of clothing, while losing a hand forces her to put a piece back on.

39831.overview: Super Speed Race Jr. is a racing arcade game that was released by Taito Corporation in 1985 only in Japan; it is the seventh and final title in their Speed Race series. The player must use a steering wheel to take up control of a car, with a single pedal to make it accelerate. The car in question is coloured red and you must guide it through the streets of a city while avoiding other CPU-controlled cars (one of which is a yellow Volkswagen Buggy), and trying not to go off the road; you will also have to watch out for zebra and level crossings as pedestrians and diesel-hauled trains pass over them.

39832.overview: Super Sprint is a racing game for one or two players, with the Arcade version allowing three players to race at the same time. Gameplay is from an overhead view of the racetrack. The racetracks start simple and gradually get more complicated, and may also feature obstacles ranging from traffic cones to tornadoes. Occasionally wrenches will appear in the roadway, and when collected they can be used after a race to power up your car with better tires, better acceleration or a higher top speed.

39838.overview:
A semi-strategic top-down tank action shooter game.

Control your tank across the battlefield and destroy all the enemies in the way and defeated the enemy fortress.

39842.overview:
This is a special edition of Super Street Fighter II that was designed for eight player tournament matches.

The core gameplay remains the same as the original game, with the main difference being that once matches finish, the winners (and losers) would move to another cabinet to fight against other players in the bracket, until all matches were completed and all players were placed in the match ranking.

The game features specialized graphics and audio that are unique to this edition, used in the attract mode, between matches, and when someone wins a tournament.

If four machines were not linked together, they could still be used as a standard Super Street Fighter II cabinet.

39863.overview: Super World Court is a tennis game and sequel to World Court. There are sixteen players to choose from: seven male, six female, as well as one robot, cat and frog. The game includes four tournaments - American Open (hard court), French Open (clay), British Open (grass) and Namco Open which features a cameo appearance by Namco's mascot Pac-Man. Singles and doubles matches (supporting up to 4 players simultaneously) are available.

39875.overview:
Super Xevious was produced by Namco in 1984.

The player controls a fighter with guns and bombs that must infiltrate a highly defended area and destroy everything in sight. The overall goal is to destroy the motherships that pop up periodically.

Super Xevious takes place on Earth. An invading alien race has set up shop, and it's up to the player to send 'em home. The game has a large number of different ground and air-based targets of either belligerent or non-belliegerent nature. In addition to the jumper-based difficulty levels, the game also adapts its difficulty to the player. If the player is successful against a type of attacker, an even deadlier type of attacker shows up to challenge the player.

The game play is very much like the original Xevious, but in this sequel, the play is a little more difficult. Several new enemies are introduced, including a silver Galaxian flagship, two jet planes, a helicopter, and a dark yellow tank.

39876.overview:
Superbike is an action game developed in 1983 by Century Electronics. 

It is essentially a shooting game that masquerades itself as a stunt bike game in which you have to jump over objects like trees, holes, and buses in order to rack up points. Plays somewhat like Moon Patrol.

39878.overview:
Super X was developed by Korean manufacturer Dooyong and published by Mitchell in 1994


A space shooter from Korean company Dooyong and published by Mitchell.

39882.overview:
'Here. You'll need this'. A modern remake of Stern Electronics' classic "Anteater", this cutesy game features boss fights, multiple entry points, an upbeat musical score and colorful graphics.

Try to eat as many pills in series as you can, as the score for every continuous next pill can become up to 1000 points per pill.

39884.overview:
Suzuka 8 Hours is an arcade game based on the famous 8 hour endurance motorbike race held on the Suzuka Circuit in Japan. Instead of racing for the full 8 hours you have to try to complete four laps against the clock on your own or against a friend. As the race is against the clock the other riders on the track are just there to overtake without crashing. Hitting another rider or an obstacle on the side of the track throws you off your bike and wastes precious seconds. The longer the race goes on the game slowly changes from racing in the day to racing at night.

Suzuka 8 Hours is viewed from a 3rd person perspective and you and a friend sit on replicas of bikes using handlebars to steer, accelerate and brake your bike.

39886.overview:
In this arcade title, the player controls SWAT, a shooting hoverboarder. The game appears to be set underwater, and each stage is almost a fixed background - though there is a tiny bit of up-and-down scrolling.

Aliens resembling sea creatures try to build a tunnel from the bottom of the stage to the top, which is your home-base.

If you touch an alien you die, and if an alien builds a tunnel right up to your home-base it gains control of it and shoots jets of fire down at you.

Besides shooting a rapid-fire laser gun, you can fire torpedoes which attach to tunnel sections and explode on a timer, allowing you to get out of range. You die if caught in the blast. Besides being able to destroy tunnel sections with your missile weapons, you can also shove them to the side.

39887.overview:
Swat Police is a single player shooting gallery video game for Arcade, created and published by ESD in 2001.

A gun shooting, horizontal scroll action game that uses joysticks and buttons rather than guns. One player can play on their own, or 2 players can team up and play simultaneously as the two SWAT police characters, Cruise and James.

39899.overview: The 'Syougi' is a Japanese chess-style game.

39998.overview:
Tengai, known as Sengoku Blade in Japan, is set in the world where magic and technology co-exist. A militaristic cult Shinrano, scheming the resurrection of their dark god, has kidnapped the Shogun's daughter Princess Futsu (Futsuhime) for a sacrifice. A group of heroes sets out to stop this evil plot. The game features branching storyline and several different endings, depending on the characters chosen.

Sengoku Blade is horizontal-scrolling shoot 'em up. The game takes place in an imaginative and futuristic version of feudal Japan featuring steam-powered machinery. The Saturn version provides an option to choose a difficulty level between 1 and 7, configure controls, and set the number of lives between 1 and 4.  The player may choose from five playable characters at the start and may unlocked two more.  Items include a power-up to increase weapon power level, bombs, and bonus coins to increase score.  Holding down the standard shot button can provide a more powerful shot.

40098.overview:
The Revenge of Shinobi, released in Japan as The Super Shinobi, is a hack-and-slash action video game developed and published by Sega in 1989. It was the first Shinobi game developed for the Sega Genesis, and was later released on the coin-operated version of that console, the Mega-Tech.

Alongside Shadow Dancer, the game is a sequel to Shinobi, and features an original score by Yuzo Koshiro. The game was included in the compilations: Mega Games 2, Mega Drive 6 Pak, Sega Classics Arcade Collection (for the Sega CD), and Sega Smash Pack (for the PC and Dreamcast). It was also re-released for the Wii Virtual Console in 2009, on the PlayStation 3 via PlayStation Network and Xbox 360 via Xbox Live Arcade download services in 2012, and for iOS and Android devices in 2017 via Sega Forever.

The game is a traditional side-scrolling platform game. The player controls Joe Musashi and must complete eight districts before the final confrontation with the head of Neo Zeed. Each district consists of three scenes, two of which are platforming levels and the third being a battle against a unique boss character.

The directional pad moves Joe around while the A, B, and C buttons are used to perform ninjutsu techniques, attack and jump, respectively. A key move in The Revenge of Shinobi is the somersault, which maximizes Joe's jumping height and enables him to throw eight shuriken at once in mid-air. Additionally, some stages consist of multiple layers, such as the first scene of the Military Base and the freeway in Area Code 818. Switching between layers is also done with the somersault move.

Alongside his standard moves and attacks, Joe has the ability to do four special ninjutsu techniques. Only one can be performed in each level, unless a ninjutsu item was picked up, or the ninjutsu of Mijin was used.

A variety of bonus crates can be found in each level, some hidden in the scenery. These include simple powerups such as extra shuriken or health packs, as well as special items to gain lives or extra ninjutsu attacks. Besides powerups, some crates may contain time bombs: explosives that detonate when their fuse runs out or if Joe comes too close (though he can walk out of the blast radius if the player is quick enough).

The game is divided into four difficulties. As difficulty increases, more enemies appear per stage; on Hardest, Joe takes twice as much damage and the number of starting lives decreases from 10 to 1. From the options menu, the player can also choose the number of starting shuriken from 0 to 90 (though a technique does exist that allows infinite shuriken). The game has two different endings, depending on whether Joe rescues his bride or not.

40105.overview: Roy Heart has been asked by the CIA to wipe out terrorists who have taken over a large skyscraper of a major auto-maker in Japan. Using your fists, knife, or gun, you must use the elevators to travel between floors and wipe out terrorists that try to bring you down. Each weapon has its disadvantages. The gun, for example, will only have so many bullets per life, and the knife will decrease in strength with every use. During your mission, you will also earn experience points, and meet and free hostages along the way. These hostages will heal you, fix your knife, and give you a machine gun. Some floors end with you defeating a boss, while others end at elevators. You must reach the top of the building where you will confront the leader.

40170.overview:
A vertical shooter where the player pilots a biplane over what is presumably the city of Tokyo. Power-ups include multiple biplanes, collect and control multiple biplanes to increase your firepower and help you to victory.

You can change the title from Japanese (Scramble Formation) to English (Tokio).

40527.overview:
Once again, inhabitants from the planet Xevious, controlled by the super-computer GAMP, are attacking the Earth, their ancient home planet, willing to re-capture it by force. The SOL towers have emerged from the ground on our planet, remotely controlled by GAMP, aiding the Xevians in their invasion. Only the brave pilots of the Solvalou aircraft are able to avert this new threat!

Super Xevious is a 2D vertically-scrolling shoot 'em up. Power-ups such as bombs, lasers, and shields can be collected; the latter protects the aircraft from immediate destruction if hit by an enemy. Other power-ups for the Solvalou include a rear shot and a bigger lock-on. Some stages are completed by fulfilling certain requirements, rather than simply proceeding, eliminating all enemies; if these are not met, the stage will loop indefinitely, sending progressively harder enemies. These objectives typically include locating and destroying a number of SOL towers; the target sight will flash when it goes over these structures.

91859.overview:
Salaryman Kintarou is an Action game, developed and published by Sammy Studios, which was released in Japan in 2004.

A video arcade mahjong game with a theme based on the Japanese manga series Salaryman Kintarō.

125633.overview: This throwback robot shoot’em up is an ode to the nostalgia of 1980s arcade games. Players will need to make strategic decisions quickly in this fast-paced, exhilarating shooter.

126403.overview:
SegaSonic Cosmo Fighter (or SegaSonic Cosmo Fighter Galaxy Patrol) is a 1993 kiddy ride that features Sonic the Hedgehog as he fights enemies in space which appear on the monitor inside the ride. The goal is to try to rescue Sonic's friends (Flicky and the gang) from Doctor Eggman. The game is shown from a top-down perspective.

There are two buttons, one for changing weapons and one for using them. There is also a lever labeled "Speed Up" which tilts the entire cabinet. Using the joystick will also tilt the cabinet. If Eggman is defeated in his giant spaceship at the end, the player will get a ship upgrade.

127865.overview:
Sonic the Hedgehog 2 is a side-scrolling platformer based around speed, and the sequel to Sonic the Hedgehog. Like the original, players run through different worlds called "zones", which each have their own specific theme. There are two Acts in nearly all of the 10 Zones, and at the end of each Zone's last Act is a machine that Robotnik controls, which you must defeat to progress.

Sonic the Hedgehog 2 was one of the games adapted for release in arcades for both the Mega-Tech and Mega Play hardware.

The Mega-Tech version is essentially the same as the Mega Drive game. Cheat codes still work and the two player mode and options screen are still present. Also, like all Mega-Tech games there is a time limit on how long the game can be played and high score table on the top screen. The time limit can be increased by inserting quarters.

The Mega Play version has a number of differences from the Mega Drive game. Cheat codes cannot be used as the Options menu is missing, time counter on the HUD has been removed completely, special stages have been removed, there are no emeralds to collect and collecting points or ring will not award the player with an extra life.

128289.overview:
Street Fighter II': Hyper Fighting is coin-op conversion of the arcade game of the same name, ported and optimized as an Xbox Live Arcade game by Sensory Sweep Studios. The original game was the second upgrade to the SF2 arcade game, and introduced faster speed, character balancing, and additional moves (e.g. mid-air hurricane kick for Ryu/Ken). There are 12 playable characters in this version: the 8 base characters along with the four bosses: Balrog, Vega, Sagat and Mr Bison.

A new mode is the Quarter Match, paying homage to the original arcade atmosphere where good players where swarmed by onlookers. Spectators can watch on-going matches and challenge the winner with virtual quarters. Other online modes include quick matches, custom matches (determine the match you want to play through a set of filters) and the possibility to create and customize your own matches. The game can also be played offline in the Arcade Mode, Vs. Mode, Training Mode, or CPU Battle. Next to the regular Live features such as messaging, leaderboards, voice chat, messaging and statistics, it also includes various achievements.

133431.overview:
Sparkz was produced by Atari Games in 1992.

A prototype Atari puzzle game where the goal is to connect the pipes at the left side of the screen to the pipes on the right hand side of the screen.

135681.overview:
Starsweep is a puzzle game for Japanese Arcades, Sony PlayStation, and Nintendo Game Boy by Japanese developer Axela, published in 1997.

The gameplay is similar to that of the Puzzle League series, but with a more traditional Tetris-like gameplay where pieces fall from the top of the screen.

Pieces come in three colors: red, yellow, and blue. Pieces commonly have a star on one end, or occasionally, a star on two ends. The aim of the game is to clear blocks from the playing field, by matching stars from same-coloured blocks. Players are rewarded for creating combos (which are called 'links') of piece clearances. The game ends when someone's piece level reaches the top of the playfield and is not cleared after three seconds.

The one player 'story' mode revolves around moving around an island and playing against opponents who gradually become harder, and consists of playing against 9 opponents (although this can be adjusted). There are also activities that involve the player concentrating on a specific task within a time limit. These include getting a high score, a high number of links, surviving for as long as possible, and clearing a field in a short time.

135713.overview:
Splendor Blast II was produced by Alpha Denshi in 1985.

Game is a cross between a driving game and a shootemup

138315.overview:
Sonic & Sega All-Stars Racing is a racing game developed by Sumo Digital. It stars characters from a wide range of Sega games, similar to the previously released Sega Superstars Tennis, also by Sumo Digital. Unlike Sega Superstars Tennis, Sonic & Sega All-Stars Racing is more skewed towards the Sonic the Hedgehog franchise, with roughly half the tracks based on the series and appoximately one third of the characters.

Its development was announced May 28, 2009, with the game being released in early 2010. It has so far been released for five home systems, including the Xbox 360, PlayStation 3, Wii, Nintendo DS, and PC. An arcade version of the game, titled Sonic & Sega All-Stars Racing Arcade and which runs on Sega's RingWide arcade hardware, was released in 2011. An iOS version was shown at E3 2011; this version is the only version of the game released in Japan.

142385.overview: Sega Golden Gun is a light gun game released by Sega in 2010 for Sega RingWide hardware. It was developed by Sega of China, by the same team responsible for the The House of the Dead series. Many of the game's assets, including the engine itself, were ported directly from The House of the Dead 4.

142391.overview:
Dive into a dream world of adventures! Climb on board this beautifully modelled dream machine and be transported to a new level of excitement. Choose your dream ride and raid as many treasures as you can whilst fending off attacks by strange and incredible enemies with your Dream Blasters.

Successfully complete your raid and be carried off into new realms in thrilling bonus stages. Nine unique dream experiences await you in this fantastic new deluxe game from Sega. Ride a dragon, pilot a UFO, get on horseback or put on your super suits and head for the skies! Dream Raiders features an exciting mix of exhilarating experiences that everyone will enjoy. The combination of intense motion, wind, sound and visuals combine to give players an arcade experience like none other!

155544.overview: Steering Champ (Handle Champ in Japan and South Korea) is a collection of car themed mini-games from Konami. The game could be described as Bishi Bashi on wheels

156388.overview:
School of Ragnarok is an online, 1 vs 1 tactical 5D fighting game from Square Enix in which players must battle each and School Guardians to come out on top!

The cabinet can link up to a second cabinet for on location battles, however, it is an online compatible machine and many matches can be played online.

Players enter the game as a student at one of the game's schools, and battle other custom characters. Players can level up their characters, get loot and item drops, and use them to keep customising their characters.

Depending on the school, the player's weapons and “school guardian” will change. Other playable school guardians include Valhallades (Fumihiko Tachiki), Lucy (Chiaki Takahashi), Urushihara Ukiyo (Yūma Uchida), and Star Cook (Tomoko Kaneda).

Mistwalker’s Kimihiko Fujisaka has designed the characters, and Monaca’s Keiichi Okabe composed the music. Square Enix game producer Takamasa Shiba and Spike Chunsoft game scenario-writer Kazutaka Kodaka are also involved in the project.

158449.overview:
Sky Challenger is a rare arcade game released by Sega in the year 2000. It operates on the classic Sega ST-V (Sega Titan Video) arcade hardware, which was famously based on the Sega Saturn console architecture.

The game is a unique flying simulator where the player controls a hang glider. The core objective revolves around a character (selectable as male or female) navigating through the air to safely land on a circular piece of terrain containing a treasure. Unlike traditional arcade flight games that use joysticks, Sky Challenger uses a trackball coupled with five buttons for its unique control scheme.

164859.overview: A fun mix tennis/squash game from Itisa Electronics.

164895.overview: SegaSonic Popcorn Shop is a popcorn vending machine. It dispenses three flavors: salted, butter, and curry. The twist: it's also an arcade game. The player chooses their flavor, then begins the minigame. Gameplay consists of turning a crank to help Tails get the corn kernels over the fire while Sonic supervises. Whether the player succeeds or not, the popcorn is microwaved and dispensed.

166629.overview: Dynamic action scenes! Split your body into three, destroy all enemies with the Invincible Fire Wheel and other new Ninja fighting techniques! Ninja Gaiden II gives you the feel of real Ninjutsu! Exciting cinema display format! Ninja Gaiden II uses the same Cinema Display Format as the original. The fiendish plot unfolds in a movie-like sequence. Action, drama, revenge. Just wait till you get to the end!

167052.overview: Space Invaders II is a fixed shooter arcade game which was released by Midway Games (in 1980); it utilizes an Intel 8080A microprocessor, running at 1.9968 MHz, and was created without authorization of Taito Corporation, who are the original creators for the Space Invaders series. Because the second official title in the series, Space Invaders Part II, was released in the U.S. as "Space Invaders Deluxe" as an update of the original, this American title was therefore given the naming of "Space Invaders II".

168431.overview:
The player controls a blue robot character named "Robop" around a 3-D perspective playfield grid, while shooting enemies and gathering items for points and beware the Inchworm it will steal your robotics hands!

Your character, Robop, must navigate his way around a playfied shooting records, snipes and bees to earn points. Gathering hamburgers, nuts, briefcases and atoms will light up the bulbs. The levels advance when all the bulbs have been lit. Robop must avoid the inchworm and pick up his hands if they become detached from his body. The game ends if all Robop hands are pushed off the screen by the inchworm or he is destroyed by the Cherry Bomb.

The left joystick moves Robop, while the right joystick fires. The joystick buttons activate Robop's Super!Charge that both speeds him up and shields him from attack.

Trivia:
Screw Loose is an unreleased prototype and was Tim Skelly's last game for Mylstar. Only 3 units were produced.

173486.overview: Super Monkey Ball: Ticket Blitz is an arcade game released as part of the Super Monkey Ball series. It is a redemption game, in which progressing through levels will give the users tickets (hence "Ticket Blitz") which would then be traded in for prizes.

179224.overview:
A 4-screen racing game released by Taito only in Japan and Europe. This is a truly exciting car race game in which the players race across four 20-inch monitors.
The game can be played by up to 4 players at the same time.  New player(s) may buy in to the race at any time. The entire race course is composed of 4 segments (4 monitors). Each of the 4 segmental courses consists of 4 different layouts and each player should choose one for his monitor. That is, there are 16 different combinations as the entire race course. In addition to the basic car function the player selects during the initial tune-up, various additional functions can be collected during the race.

Up to 4 people can play at the same time. If a position is available, anybody can join in the race (The game allows players to compete with each other or against the computer). Insert coin and press the start button. Before each race starts, each participant is asked to choose a course pattern
for his monitor. Turn the steering wheel to find your favorite pattern and press the select button.

The race consists of 9 sub-divided races: DRAG race, 1st- 7th races and FINAL race. All races have various obstacles. lying in wait. * After the DRAG race, players can choose a special function for his car according to the following (Use the wheel and button to choose):
increase maximum speed fast acceleration TURBO ENGINE
SUSPENSION super grip tires BODY increases body strength Cover the specified lap within the time on display and clear each race. During the race, you see various function marks lying on the course. Collect them to super-charge your car. If you collect all of the function marks, you car becomes an almighty super-car. However, upon explosion or falling into the water, the car function reverts back to the initial setting. If you fail to reach the goal before the timer reads "0", you are out.

180646.overview:
An unlicensed arcade multi-game with 8 space invaders themed games including:  
Space Invaders 
Space Invaders Deluxe
Lunar Rescue
Balloon Bomber
Jatre Specter 
Space Laser
Galaxy Wars
Super Earth Invasion

186984.overview: Sushi Bar is a puzzle game for the Sammy Atomiswave arcade board. The gameplay is very similar with Puyo Puyo where the player must rearrange various foods of the traditional Japanese culinary to unlock the next level. The game was released only in Japan.

187180.overview: A video fitness machine developed in 1997 by Gaelco for Salter Fitness for their stepper machine. The machine has no audio.

189903.overview:
In Super Hang-On you race a motorcycle around the world, completing each section of track within a time limit. There are other bikes on the road, but beating this is not important, so they can be thought of as moving obstacles. Each continent is a different difficulty level: Africa is beginner, Asia is junior, the Americas are senior, and Europe is expert.

This is a very simple and straightforward game, viewed from behind the bike in 2D (so the screen does not tilt with the bike). The right/left controls are steering, and up/down are gear changes. Your cycle is always moving, and your speed strictly depends on the gear you are in, although contact or running off the road slows the bike down.

The Sega Genesis version features "Original mode" in which the player participates in racing tournaments, hires mechanics, upgrades his bike. This mode uses passwords allowing players to continue a previously played game.

191744.overview:
Space Battleship Yamato (宇宙戦艦ヤマト Uchū Senkan Yamato) was a 1985 Japanese exclusive Laserdisc video game designed by Taito.  The game is based on the anime Japanese science fiction television series of the same name. Although not released in North America, the game shows two title screens, one in Japanese and another in English. The English title screen uses the Star Blazers: Space Cruiser Yamato naming used for the anime series broadcast on North American and Australian television

The arcade game is unrelated to the Star Blazer Sega game released in 1983. The arcade game features footage from the movies and series as well as  original animation created solely for the purpose of this laser disc game. The game play is a hybrid of different laser disc genres. It is mainly a collection of firing stages similar to Astron Belt and Cobra Command. It also has action sequences similar to those found in games like Ninja Hayate or Dragon's Lair.

204515.overview:
Senjin Aleste features a new gameplay system compared to previous titles, with the player having access to four different ships and being able to swap between them during gameplay, with each ship having its own unique weapons. Lives are tied to the ships, with each ship counting as one life, the game ending when all four ships are lost. Downed ships are revived over time, however, indicated by four meters at the bottom corresponding to each ship.

The game features four difficulty levels: Novice, Casual, Original and Expert, with each difficulty changing the amount of bullets fired by enemies and the respawn time for downed ships.

205564.overview:
Super Alpine Racer
This remake of the arcade classic comes with brand new characters and completely redesigned courses. In collaboration with Raw Thrills, Super Alpine Racer has a vertically mounted 55″ HD monitor. There are multi-colored LEDs infused into t-moldings of the cabinet! The multi-pivot platform simulates the movements of a downhill skier. Feel the wind through your hair from the built-in air blowers and shoot through the gates to gain an additional boost to speed past your opponents while performing insane tricks in the air.

210407.overview:
Super Bubble Bobble MD is an unlicensed Sega Mega Drive game, released in 1995 and most likely developed by Gamtec. As the name suggests, it is an unlicensed attempt at mimicking the formula of Taito Bubble Bobble.

The game allows the user to play as Bub and Cororon, as well as anime characters Crayon Shin-chan and Doraemon.

In 1996, an arcade version was released by Sun Mixing, called Super Bubble Bobble. The arcade version is slightly different: it only has Bub (P1) and Cororon (P2) as playable characters, and you select which round you want to play instead of selecting a character.

213526.overview: SOUND VOLTEX BOOTH is a rhythm game developed by Konami and released on January 18, 2012. It is the first entry of the SOUND VOLTEX series.

218852.overview: Spider-Man: Homecoming is an “endless runner” style game in which the player controls Spider-Man against the Vulture. Run or websling along a path until confronting the Vulture. He can be beaten via button taps, and the player can win the ticket/coupon jackpot. The cabinet has a colorful design that departs from Adrenaline’s usual style and it supports 2 players at the same time.

233203.overview: Real Puncher is an incredibly rare, strength-testing sports arcade game released by Taito in 1994. Acting as the arcade sequel to the famous Sonic Blast Man franchise, it combined physical punching mechanics with early interactive video features.

418340.overview: Sonic Dash Extreme is an arcade version of the mobile phone game, Sonic Dash, developed by Sega Amusements and released by Sega. An arcade version became available in selected places in the United Kingdom on May 2015. The arcade version features daily and all-time leaderboards and different control methods for large-sized d-pad controllers.

419231.overview:
Sega are the undisputed masters of the arcade game; the brains behind Sonic and Tails. Despite having stepped out of the home console market, Sega remains a major player in the video game industry, with arcade machines at the heart of its business. This epic twin seat driving game offers a realistic, competitive experience, as two petrolheads battle it out behind the wheel.

Showdown is a full octane game that takes in breathtaking scenery based on real life locations in the USA and Japan, blended with classic cars with tons of character. From pick-up trucks to funeral hearses, the handling on this machine is spectacular, and it gives the players a real connection with the events on screen. Each gamer will have to jump, swerve, overtake and find new routes in order to come out on top of their opponents.

In Race Off mode, drivers are free to go where they like; Demolition mode changes all that, and players have to destroy opponents' vehicles before they come back with a vengeance. In Knockout mode, speed is the key element: it's a no-rules joyride to the chequered flag. Crossroads takes drivers through a series of intersections; one poses the very real risk of being run right off the circuit.

This machine has integrated 42" LCD monitors for immersive play, plus an in-game radio station. One twin machine can be linked to another for four-player fun.

419530.overview:
A quiz game where players are greeted by anime high school girls. The player is asked a multiple choice question, the player answers using one of the 4 buttons on the control panel. Each button corresponds to A,B,C or D.

There is a time limit on questions, a correct answer pleases the girl a wrong question angers the girl and causes the player to lose a life point. The game can be play as either solo or with a friend.

419823.overview: A 2D fighting game spin-off from the Koihime Musou franchise, where where the generals of the Romance of the Three Kingdoms have been reimagined as anime heroines.

420298.overview: Using a cue ball, you roll the ball into the machine. An IR sensor reads where the ball rolls, and knocks down pins accordingly. There are variations of bowling including regular bowling, Strike or Die and Flash.

422156.overview:
Starwing Paradox is a multiplayer arcade game in which two teams of eight players each pilot giant humanoid mechs in a battle to control the playing field and assault the opposing team's base. The object of the game is to destroy the opposing team's core, which is protected by a barrier that can only be brought down by capturing three of the five neutral objectives, known as ports, on the map.

In addition to the standard flying, shooting and sword-fighting actions expected of mech combat, the players' mechs can enter a high-speed "Full Drive" mode to move between objectives in a matter of seconds. Prior to each game, players can customize their mechs with an assortment of weapons and head/body/limb models to suit their play style and role within the team. Players can save their mech setups to a user account maintained by Square Enix.

Starwing Paradox was developed and published by Square Enix with animation produced by Sunrise.

422193.overview: Shining Force Cross Exlesia is an an update to Shining Force Cross Raid.

443052.overview:
Solitaire is a unique redemption and card arcade game developed and released in South Korea by F2 System Ltd. in March 1999. Long considered lost or "undumped" by arcade preservationists, the game's code was successfully dumped and newly emulated in MAME in October 2023.

Unlike a standard home computer version of the card game, this arcade version was adapted for the coin-op environment with several distinct traits:

• The Attract Mode: The game is well-known in retro-gaming circles for featuring a notably bizarre, pre-rendered 3D model during its attract loop.
• Adult/Nudity Settings: Built into the operator's service menu is a selectable level of nudity (which defaults to "casual"). Progressing through the stages yields various "prizes" or image reveals based on this setting.
• Hardware Boot: Running on South Korean F2 System hardware, the machine initializes with a prominent "SELF TEST" screen upon boot-up, runs a comprehensive hardware diagnostic check, and then loads the game software.

443110.overview: SOUND VOLTEX EXCEED GEAR is the highly popular sixth major installment in Konami’s premier Bemani rhythm game franchise. Designed to simulate an high-energy, electronic disc jockey experience, players interact with objects falling down a simulated corridor using a specialized control panel. It features an extensive soundtrack consisting of upbeat otaku dance music, J-Core, Vocaloid tracks, VTuber music, and fan-submitted remixes.

448113.overview: Shakatto Tambourine! Cho PowerUp Chu! (シャカっとタンバリン！超PowerUpチュッ！) is a rhythm game developed and published by Sega for the Sega NAOMI GD-ROM arcade system. It is an update to Shakatto Tambourine! 2001, which was the sequel to Shakatto Tambourine!.

450357.overview:
The concept of the game revolves around a team of super heroes kids lead by the commander Dory and three action hero named Kimpo, Sosa, and Ice. All them have a unique main weapon: Bubble Gun, Boomerangs, and Alien Discs, respectively. They receive a request for help from animals through the different stages which always lead to an enemy boss at the end of the level.

The game is played with a trackball, you only need to aim, there no button for shooting, the only button in the cabinet is used for dodge enemies (boss) bullets. After you beat a boss there will be recap showing how many animals you rescued and a rating at the end (with tickets if enabled).

There are 3 different scenes, but they must be selected by the operator using the dipswitches, Volcano, Jungle Heaven and Ice Cream Mountain. Every stage has different animals to rescue, different enemies, a different boss and different heroes to play.

454359.overview: Sailor Zombie: AKB48 Arcade Edition is based on a Japanese TV series called Sailor Zombie that tells the story of schoolgirls trying to survive in a post-apocalyptic world overrun by zombies. In Sailor Zombie: AKB48 Arcade Edition players must either shoot the other AKB48 members that have been transformed into zombies or inject an antidote to the members, as well as fight Big Bad Bosses. As you progress, Sailor Zombie: AKB48 Arcade Edition suddenly turns into a rhythm game, with the zombie schoolgirls dancing to AKB48 tunes.

454855.overview:
Sonic Blast Heroes is a new punch machine with improved safety features. It features 5 advanced video stages. The player punches the pad as hard as possible to knock away the enemies. Modes include VS Bank Robber, VS Trailer, VS Dinosaur, VS Kraken, VS Meteor.

This punch machine can be played from 2 to 4 players.

454944.overview: Street Fighter IV (ストリートファイター IV, Sutorīto Faitā Fō) is a 2008 arcade fighting game developed by Capcom and Dimps and published by Capcom.[8] It was the first original main entry in the series since Street Fighter III in 1997, a hiatus of eleven years. Designed for the Taito Type X2 hardware, it was ported with additional features in 2009 to PlayStation 3, Xbox 360 and Windows, along with mobile versions later on.

464529.overview: Shanghai IV: Ryūmon Hiyaku, the sub-title loosely translated to "Dragon Gate Leap", is a mahjong solitaire game developed and released by Success (under license from Sunsoft) for arcades digitally via the ALL.Net P-ras MULTI Version 3 service for Sega's PC-based ALLS UX hardware on March 16, 2023. It is the fourth numbered arcade installment of the Shanghai series of mahjong solitaire games, bringing it back to its traditional roots with a single no-gimmick single-player game mode. It features both standard arcade controls (with a button to help speed up the cursor) and touchscreen controls. Players progress through 20 stages of unique layouts and are scored based on their speed, with a global leaderboard for those using their supported IC card. As with traditional arcade games in the series, players have a countdown timer to work against (which replenishes on matches) and multiple assist power-ups to work with (including one to automatically match a a pair, one to peek under tiles, and one to show all available matches). Completing stages 5, 10, and 15 throws players into a bonus mini-game based on concentration to earn additional power-ups and score.

464709.overview: This upgrade kit for the very popular Star Wars: Battle Pod arcade game features the brand new and exciting “Battle of Takodana” level. This exhilarating level lets you repel the first order’s attack on Maz Kanata’s castle located on Takodana as seen in Star Wars Episode VII: The Force Awakens. Jump into the cockpit of an X-wing fighter and fly alongside Poe Dameron to help the rebel alliance defeat the villainous first order’s TIE fighters. This action packed level will require that you use all your senses to pilot your way through the battle that unfolds around you while you’re seated in the cockpit of the enormous projected dome screen of the Star Wars: Battle Pod.

465748.overview:
The game challenges players by presenting puzzles that require arranging numbers in specific sequences. The mechanics are designed to be intuitive, providing a learning curve that caters to both beginners and more seasoned players. The interface is user-friendly, allowing for quick adaptation and prolonged engagement.

While it might not have gained massive mainstream attention, the title holds a special place for fans of classic puzzle games. It showcases the creativity and skill of IGS during a time when the company was making strides in the gaming industry, offering diverse entertainment options during the golden age of arcade gaming.

465749.overview: Shamisen Brothers is an obscure arcade rhythm game developed by Kato's, a company which otherwise mainly developed prize and medal games. The gameplay consists of strumming a shamisen to the rhythm of various popular songs, from enka to J-pop.

466724.overview:
SKYCURSER is a frantic, hard-action shoot ‘em up drawing crowds of players at arcades and across the globe. Available today as a dedicated cabinet or JAMMA conversion kit, SKYCURSER is an exciting new chapter in arcade gaming’s rich history.

The year is 1996. A cataclysmic plague descends on earth. As its infection spreads, hope fades. But you and your dog fight back. Piloting the prophetic weapon, SKYCURSER, you take flight to destroy the Necrostar’s mutant hordes and save the planet.

468900.overview:
Side by Side 2 Evoluzione RR is an arcade racing video game developed and published by Taito in May 1997. Running on the Taito JC System arcade hardware, it represents the definitive final revision (Version 3.1 J) of the Side by Side 2 game software.

The game focuses heavily on Japanese touge (mountain pass) time trials and street racing, featuring licensed tuner cars from major Japanese manufacturers—serving as a direct spiritual predecessor to Taito's later Battle Gear franchise.

482538.overview:
The Spectre Files: Deathstalker is an incredibly rare, "long-lost" live-action FMV (Full-Motion Video) arcade game originally developed in 1984–1985 by legendary designer Brian Colin (creator of Rampage and Discs of Tron). Initially shelved by Bally Midway right on the cusp of completion due to the collapse of the laserdisc market, the game was rescued from obscurity decades later and officially finished and manufactured by Galloping Ghost Productions in 2018.

Modeled as a cheesy, wacky B-movie style 1950s noir horror story. You play as a supernatural private eye investigating an abandoned mansion (the "Durborow Institute") to find a missing blonde.
